root_cause: The bias addition needed prior to clamping (`src[n] + 0x80`) was implemented using ordinary 32-bit int arithmetic without first widening the operands, so extreme decoded sample values (which are only bounds-checked after the addition, inside av_clip_uint8) can overflow signed 32-bit int range before the clamp has a chance to bound them.
findings: In the OSQ audio decoder's sample-format conversion loop for AV_SAMPLE_FMT_U8P, the decoded 32-bit sample `src[n]` is added to 0x80 before being clamped with av_clip_uint8(). Because `src[n]` is a plain `int32_t` and `0x80` is interpreted as a regular `int` literal, the addition `src[n] + 0x80` is performed using signed 32-bit int arithmetic.
